headline: Cannabis medicine calms agitation in dementia patients

sources.title: Combination of THC and CBD significantly reduced agitation in people with late-stage dementia
Clinical Trial: THC-CBD Formulation Reduces Agitation in Dementia Patients, With Nearly 90% Showing Improvement
Agitation improves in Alzheimer's disease with combined CBD, THC treatment

chunks.text: Scientists have {{come up with}} a new medicine that may bring relief to people with late-stage [[dementia]]. The medicine carefully mixes two [[compounds]] from the cannabis plant, known as THC and CBD. Doctors tested it on patients who often deal with [[agitation]], a state of restlessness and distress. In early results that just {{came out}}, the treatment {{calmed down}} many patients.

chunks.text: The researchers {{went about}} the LiBBY trial with great care, testing about 120 people whose dementia was very advanced. Their average age was 80, and most were eligible for [[hospice]] care. Nurses {{handed out}} the medicine as a fast-acting oil that patients could swallow. For 12 weeks, the team {{kept track of}} how each person's [[behavior]] and mood changed.

chunks.text: The results {{turned out}} to be very strong. Close to 90 percent of the patients on the medicine got better, while far fewer improved on a [[placebo]]. That large gap made the study {{jump out}} at other researchers. One lead doctor said it is rare to see so many patients [[respond]] so well to a new drug.

chunks.text: Still, the researchers {{spell out}} that this is a controlled medical treatment, not the same as [[recreational]] cannabis products sold in stores. The medicine was made in a lab and given under close [[supervision]]. Side effects were mild, and doctors could not {{rule out}} that some were caused by the illness itself. As they {{look ahead}}, the team hopes larger trials will confirm these hopeful results.
